note.question: Would you like to upgrade to a premium room?
note.overview: An important challenge faced by hotels is how to set their premium room price differential over their standard rooms and how to manage the upsell process. Standby upgrades, where the customer is only charged if the upgrade is available at the time of arrival, is one technique that has become increasingly popular in practice for monetizing the premium room inventory that may otherwise go unused. The paper develops a model of premium room and standby upgrade pricing under an uncertain market size and examine how and when standby upgrades can provide additional revenue for a hotel.

conditions: If the premium room demand, DP, turns out to be greater than the premium room capacity, this would be equivalent to a real-life scenario of a premium room sell-out before the end of the selling horizon.

After observing the demand for premium rooms, DP, and the demand for standby upgrades, DS, the hotel uses a random allocation policy for the premium room capacity if the number of remaining premium rooms is less than the number of the standby upgrades requested.

At the beginning of the selling horizon for a specific day-of-stay, based on the market size expectation, the hotel determines a fixed premium room differential, p, and standby upgrade price, pS, that is pegged to the standard room price (s) throughout the selling horizon.
